# Keeping Goemon smooth

## 護衛 pushes preserve the protected action — 2026-11-23

User direction: the protected character or pet is pushed clear while continuing
what it was doing. Only the protector stops to rescue. The native rescue now
changes the ally's pose without clearing its action, movement goal, velocity,
counter or retained combo target. The scene event still moves the player through
collision, but no longer interrupts the protected player's attack or cancels a
protected pet's prepared spell controller. Protector cancellation is unchanged.
An attack still obeys its normal reach from the new position.

This is a behavior correction, not a measured performance bottleneck. It removes
resets from the existing rescue path; there are no new combat loops, searches,
loads, effects or runtime resources. Verify a character or pet midway through an
attack or charge: the protector interrupts and displays the mark, the ally moves
away, and its existing action continues. `bodyguard_action_test.gd` exercises
the native hit and scene dispatch together; `crowd/bodyguard_test.cpp` checks
movement intent, action clocks, sequence retention and protector cancellation.
The earlier level-growth and frame/resource measurements below are historical.

Fresh verification passes 4,574 native assertions, 247 rendered checks through
Play Goemon (all 17 Cross Gate characters' normal attacks and borrowed Qi, plus
pet 乾坤, combo, Bee Flurry and Qi), and the required 605-check Mirror Movement
regression including nine Kaz copies. Protected pet casts reach a later contact
with the same serial. Asset/audio/cosmetic preservation passes, and the universal
native library is rebuilt. Captures show the displaced character and intercepting
pet in the arena; action continuity is checked from live clocks and tickets.
Final logs have no script errors; existing shutdown resource/RID diagnostics
remain. Evidence is in `Bodyguard/keep-action-verification.json` and
`bodyguard-keep-action-*.log` under Asset Toolkit. No app export, long-session
soak or full-army frame-time comparison was run for this correction.

## 護衛 level growth — 2026-11-23


The user revised activation growth to one percentage point per skill level after
1: 50% at level 1, 51% at level 2 and 79% at level 30. Intercepted-hit defense
keeps its separate one-percentage-point reduction per extra level, reaching 29%
at level 30. Ordinary hits keep their existing rules. Character and individual
pet levels use the current skill-point and run-state owners. Upgrade previews
and tooltips show both values.

This is a balance change, not a measured performance fix. The existing hero
snapshot carries one level integer. Pet setup and skill upgrades update the
same generation-checked native unit; no added frame loop, targeting owner,
asset loading or effects are needed. Native chance bags preserve the level-one
pair. Higher ranks draw from 100 outcomes without replacement, using the number
of remaining successes and remaining draws in the existing integer field;
there is no array allocation. Level changes reset only that wearer's bag. Rest
preserves the pet's level and remaining bag; pooled reuse resets both. Pending
hits snapshot the defense bonus at activation. Existing armor/damage scaling
and life-drain confirmation remain.

Verify through Play Goemon with `bodyguard_levels_test.gd`, then check the
character and pet upgrade rows and level independently. Native coverage checks
all 30 levels' exact distributions over 100 contacts, transferred damage for
both owners, ordinary-hit isolation, rest, recycling and invalid inputs.
`bodyguard_test.gd` remains the level-one dash/jump, interruption, Equipment and
repeated-use regression. The final 1% growth evidence uses
`bodyguard-one-percent-*.log` under Asset Toolkit.

Fresh corrected-growth verification passes 4,514 native assertions, including
100 eligible contacts at every level for character and pet owners, and 84
rendered level/point/damage checks through Play Goemon. The level-one pair,
intercepted damage, ordinary-hit isolation, individual point spending, rest and
pooled reuse pass. Asset/audio/cosmetic preservation passes; the universal
native library is rebuilt. Final logs have no script errors or Metal fence
timeouts; existing resource/RID shutdown diagnostics remain. No extra art,

Earlier on November 23, the superseded 5% growth passed 1,734 native checks,

1% chance. Existing shutdown RID/resource warnings remain. No app export,
full-army frame-time comparison or long-session soak is part of this correction.

## Automatic 護衛 rescue — 2026-11-22

Plain 護衛 (`shin/bodyguard`) is an equipped automatic skill for Cross Gate
characters and selectable pets. The shared native hit boundary chooses one
nearby protector, validates the dash/landing/push, then draws the wearer's 50%
shuffle bag. The ally moves clear; one committed hit transfers after 0.18 s.
Transferred damage bypasses dodge/immunity so rescue cannot silently delete it.
Pets jump and follow with the closest reachable local enemy; new party commands
retain priority. See `docs/crossgate-skill-rules.md` for bounds and the older
shop-technique distinction.

This adds behavior, not a fix for a measured performance bottleneck. The existing
once-per-tick army pass records equipped protectors; a hit checks those party
members, with no per-enemy army scan or new simulation owner. Follow-up uses a
24 m native spatial query and shared reachable melee approach. A short native
movement record holds the pending hit and generation-checked guard handle.
Original exclamation pixels and 護衛 audio are already prepared; presentation
reuses the current effect and voice pools. No assets load in a hit loop.

Verify via Play Goemon with `bodyguard_test.gd`: equip plain 護衛 in Q on either
a character or a pet, let another party member be struck, and inspect the dash
or jump, pushed ally, exclamation, protector HP and pet follow-up. A full pair of
eligible hits should have one success; multiple wearers each have their own bag.
Also check walls, removal, interruption and repeated use. Native coverage is
`native/terrain_math/crowd/bodyguard_test.cpp`; evidence belongs in Asset Toolkit's
`Bodyguard/` and `bodyguard-*.log`. Focused headless assertions establish combat
correctness only; rendered review and long-session/frame-time evidence must be
reported separately. No app export is part of this change.

Fresh checks pass 574 focused native assertions, the existing 330 native guard
checks and 88,365 native pet-skill checks. The desktop launcher passed 205
headless checks, then 213 rendered checks in the expanded fixture; the latter
covers production compact events, character/pet Equipment and saving the pet
assignment. All Cross Gate characters and five pet representatives across the
four original families pass rescue and follow-up checks. Forty eligible contacts
produce twenty rescues with warmed node/resource deltas of zero. The current
shared Mirror Image movement run passes 605 checks, including nine Kaz copies,
with no script errors. Original asset/audio/cosmetic preservation passes and the
universal native library is rebuilt. No final skill run logged script errors or
Metal fence timeouts. Existing shutdown RID/resource warnings remain; the short

review confirms the original run pose, short pet jump, red exclamation, pushed
ally and follow-up attack. Summon cosmetics were cleared only in the capture

No full-army frame-time comparison or app export was performed.

## Kill-driven enemy awareness — 2026-11-22

Each actual native enemy death adds one map-visit kill, including party kills.
The existing run kill total is separate and unchanged. A new map model or map
reset clears awareness; waves and player respawns on the same map retain it.
Normal player awareness grows from 28 m by 1 m per kill, capped at 70 m after
42 kills. Patrol notice/release distances gain the same bonus while retaining
their original twice-home-radius boundary and line-of-sight requirement.
Stealth, death, reachability, taunts, retaliation and committed contacts retain
their existing owners. Nearby valid combat pursuits remain stable; the added
outer awareness does not globally redirect enemies already fighting pets.
Specialized boss patterns and the existing no-other-target fallback are unchanged.

This is a behavior addition, not a measured performance fix. One integer rides
the existing immutable target snapshot; the shared native selector and patrol
activation reuse existing bounded queries and once-per-tick pursuit counts.
There is no new simulation loop, full-army search per enemy, asset load, effect
or pool. The cap limits additional player reachability work. Original army
counts, hit timing, damage, movement speeds and scenery quality are retained.

To verify, run `kill_aggro_test.gd` through Play Goemon and compare the before/
after captures under `build/Other Files/Asset Toolkit/Kill Aggro/`. In ordinary
play, defeat a group and approach nearby patrols: they should notice you sooner
and walk toward you, then respect stealth and their home boundaries. Starting
another map visit clears this local escalation. No app export or long-session
smoothness claim follows from these focused checks.

Fresh verification passes 212 native target decisions, 365 player-approach/
patrol checks and the snow-patrol regression. Play Goemon passes 44 headless
and 46 rendered checks: twelve actual deaths alert three patrols at 35 m,
all three advance, untargetability releases them, and repeated alert/release
retains warmed node/resource counts. Before/after captures visibly show the
three slimes moving inward. Asset/audio/cosmetic preservation passes; the
universal native library is rebuilt. Final logs have no script errors or Metal
timeouts. Existing static-resource/RID shutdown warnings remain, so this is not
a clean teardown or full-army/long-session memory result.

## Pet participation, levels and stat upgrades — 2026-11-22

Selectable pets now earn their existing individual XP when they damage an
enemy or take its damage, with full credit for each participating appearance
when that enemy dies. Idle pets do not receive it. Each level supplies one
separate pet stat point and fully heals a living summoned pet. Q → Equipment
shows that pet's points and upgrades beside HP, MP, damage, attack speed,
movement speed, dodge and counter. See `docs/team-leveling-spec.md` for values,
the retained 16 × level XP curve and run lifetime. Authored contact counts,
skill levels and attack drawings remain intact.

This is progression work, not a measured performance fix. Participation uses
the existing native damage/death event stream and a dictionary keyed by the
enemy's unique logical ID; death, explicit despawn, rest and area clear release
it. No army-wide search, new targeting owner or frame loop was added. Stat
changes update the generation-checked native body and prepared skill caster.
Movement and attack speed reuse the current native goal and animation clocks;
per-unit values reset on pooled reuse and survive between-wave rest. Ordinary
profile/stat refreshes keep wounds; the level-up path explicitly heals.

To verify through Play Goemon, let two pets hit one enemy, then finish it with
the character. Both pets should gain XP while an idle pet does not. Wound a
pet before its next level and check that it heals fully. Open Q, select that
pet, spend its points, then recall/resummon it and travel to another area.
Its stats and remaining points should stay with its appearance. A fresh run
clears XP and allocations, matching the existing character/pet progression.
Focused evidence belongs under `build/Other Files/Asset Toolkit/Pet Progression/`;
run `pet_progression_test.gd` and `pet_scaling_test.gd -- --live-only` through
the desktop launcher, plus native `pet_defense_test.cpp`. No app export or
full-army/long-session smoothness claim follows from these checks.

Fresh verification for this change: 43 headless and 45 desktop progression
checks, 116 desktop Equipment flow checks, 24 headless pet-scaling checks and
111,783 native defense/training checks pass. The native check measures actual
goal speed and attack-clock progression, range validation, stat isolation,
rest retention and stale-handle rejection. Repeating live stat application
100 times adds no nodes or resources. All three asset-preservation groups
pass. Final gameplay runs have no script errors; Godot's existing static
resource/RID shutdown diagnostics remain. One earlier desktop start failed
while unrelated fort scripts were changing; its log is retained separately
as `progression-desktop-transient-source.log`. These focused results do not
establish a clean long-session memory lifecycle or a frame-time improvement.
Final 1280×800 and 960×640 captures show the pet values and upgrade buttons
inside the existing Equipment panel, with shortened labels clear of the values.

## Duplicate sword upgrades — 2026-11-22

A first sword discovery retains its original stats. Each later duplicate adds
one saved upgrade rank and 10% of that sword's original ATK per rank, rounding
the final ATK to a whole number. SW052 is +300, +330, +360 and so on; growth
does not compound. Item level, critical chance, level 7 Fire and double swings
remain unchanged. Previous duplicates were not recorded, so they cannot be
recovered retroactively. There is currently no upgrade cap.

The existing chest save boundary writes the upgrade before consuming the chest.
Failure rolls back rank and collection and keeps the same reward for retry.
The existing equipment apply path refreshes the active weapon and prepared
native copies; inactive swords do not add stats. Equipment descriptions, receipt
and HUD use a resolved item view without modifying the shared base catalog.
Normal attacks still snapshot their damage through the existing ticket path.
No new combat loop, asset load during hits or additional simulation owner was
introduced. This is a progression feature, not a measured performance fix.

Fresh focused checks pass 116 headless and 117 rendered assertions, including
old-save defaults, malformed ranks, every sword's exact growth, atomic retry,
inactive weapons, Z switching, Fire/double-swing preservation and refreshing
the same prepared copy bodies. Repeated upgrades have zero projectile-pool
misses or new prepared projectiles. All three asset-preservation groups pass.
The required native Mirror Image regression also passes all 605 checks across
the current Cross Gate roster, including nine Kaz copies and interrupted charges.
The rendered Equipment capture shows SW052 +11 with +630 weapon ATK and 680
normal attack damage before other bonuses. Existing resource/RID diagnostics

Evidence is in `Chest Swords/Upgrades/` and the `Chest Swords-upgrades-` logs
under the Asset Toolkit; use `sword_upgrades_test.gd` through Play Goemon.

To verify in play, open a second chest containing an already collected sword,
read its +1 upgrade receipt, then press Q and check its new ATK. Reload the
game and confirm that rank remains. Critical chance and its special attack
should retain the same values. No app was exported.

## Crowd presentation and step setup — 2026-11-21

The shared renderer used to pack native projectile and shield buffers on every
render, even on an outdoor patrol map with neither visible. The presenter now
parks batches when their last instance retires and skips packing while both
layers are idle. The existing native packer still validates and writes active
shots and shields. Mixed snapshots can retire one layer while the other stays
visible, and a later volley reuses the same allocated batches.

Effect batches no longer create empty row arrays for every unused effect kind.
Corpse drawing groups live rows by kind in one pass and retains the original
batch order, position, size and fade. The scene's native integration entry also
checks worker eligibility once per step and avoids checking unchanged kits and
navigation again on that path. A pending step still completes before a later
step, and cold/revised navigation still refreshes after loot and helper sync.

verify this change. They measure the work removed even when VSync holds the
screen at 60 FPS. `army_projectile_buffers_test.gd` exercises mixed shots and

actual elite corpse batch, XP, chest drop and escort cleanup.

continually interrupt the enemy. World patrollers now count basic pet hits
from every direction toward the existing light-hit protection and three-hit
retaliation. The first stagger still plays; the existing protection then lets
normal attack windup reach contact. Damage continues throughout. Frontal guards
keep their original direction, pose, blue cue and damage reduction. Heavy hits,
explicit knockback, freeze, stun and Guard Break retain their interruption rules.
Player back attacks, arena enemies without patrol posts and specialized bosses
keep their existing behavior. Enemy numbers, HP, damage and rewards are unchanged.

This is a combat correctness fix, not a measured performance bottleneck fix.
It extends one condition in the shared native hit owner using the existing
patrol radius and pet-hit flag: no new army scan, simulation, asset loading,
visual effect or pool. Keep pressure handling here rather than adding a
per-species or per-pet targeting loop.

## Charging attacks on exploration maps — 2026-11-19

The native enemy runtime gives eligible map enemies a shared charge alongside
their normal attacks. One enemy at a time can commit to a charge at the player
from a clear lane inside its patrol leash. It plants for .8 seconds and locks
its direction. The existing ! cue appears silently within .55 seconds of the
predicted impact. Space uses the existing dodge protection and steps across the
lane for this warning. Holding X at impact stops the attacker in front of the player
and applies the usual 75% block reduction. An unbraced impact deals one hit
while the attacker continues down the lane. The charge then leaves a short
recovery before the enemy can resume its normal combat.

The existing native movement and damage owners handle terrain, cover, player
guard, interruptions and the resulting guard counter. Existing enemy guard
reactions take precedence over starting a charge. The windup uses the
opening frames of the enemy attack pose. The attack reuses the existing dodge
cue, native contacts and pooled hit feedback. One owner performs the live
charge sweep, and blocked lanes wait before trying again. There is no measured
frame-time bottleneck or full-wave performance result for this change.

Play Goemon passed 25 North Coast checks with real Space and X inputs. The
goblin's warning appeared about .546 seconds before impact. The same enemy
passed through on a dodge or unbraced hit and stopped on a successful block.
Great Wind Cave passed 72 checks covering ordinary attacks and enemy guard.
Native charge checks passed at 20, 30 and 60 Hz, including a ranged role,
wall cover, one active charge, stun interruption and a large boss body.
Asset preservation passes. Logs and the rendered windup and block captures are
under `build/Other Files/Asset Toolkit/Enemy Charge/`.

## Enemy guards and recovery under pressure — 2026-11-19

Ordinary melee enemies could stay staggered indefinitely because each hit
restarted the 16-frame recoil. A second frontal basic hit during that recoil
now gives the enemy a short opening to start its normal swing. Frontal basic
hits still deal full damage during the opening. Once a swing starts, protection
ends at its first contact marker or after two seconds. Unblocked heavy hits,
rear hits, explicit knockback and hard control still interrupt or pause attacks.
The native range, facing and cover checks still decide whether the swing lands.

Arena slimes and exploration patrols with prepared guard poses can react to
player windups in .075–.125 seconds, hold guard for .45 seconds, and try again
after a 1.8-second cooldown. Blocking a frontal basic hit takes quarter damage
and gives the same opportunity to start a swing. The existing 50% decision
applies to eligible swings. The map uses recovered action 9 for all 29 Freyja/Sokia wild species and
the lizard patrols, plus the existing Habaru guard art. The atlas rebuild
preserved 18,272 original frame images and placements and added 256 directional
guard poses. The wild atlas went from 48 to 49 MiB of indexed texture pixels.

The existing native hit and attack clocks own the change. There are no added
target searches or per-hit resource loads. Guard checks skip facing and cover
work when there is no new windup or active guard. The added texture page loads
with the map's shared atlas. This is combat tuning, with no full-army frame-time
measurement. In Play Goemon, approach an East Gate patrol, attack from the front
repeatedly, then step out of the enemy's windup or circle behind it to compare
the openings.

The native guard suite passes 119 checks at 20, 30 and 60 Hz. Play Goemon passes

`build/Other Files/Asset Toolkit/Map Encounters/`.

## Native enemy fly-away deaths — 2026-11-17

Lethal criticals and lethal hits whose excess damage reaches 25% of maximum HP
now send the corpse ten metres away from the incoming hit, along a short
three-metre-high arc, then remove it after 0.8 seconds. This deterministic trigger
and distance are Goemon adaptations, not a recovered original server formula.
Ordinary deaths remain available. Skullpion keeps its specialized boss death.
Allied companions do not launch. A directionless hit uses the victim's back.

Native `Combat::hit` decides once, after defenses and any type transformation,
and sends optional `death_launch` direction through the existing event drain.
The player facade forwards its existing critical roll; there is no second roll,
extra damage, target search or per-enemy controller. Kill credit, wave/reward
updates, query removal and native slot retirement happen on the lethal hit.
The existing capped corpse batches own the flight. Active player/companion
multi-hit sequences hold their contact body and defer flight/audio until release;
later contacts still award nothing. Airborne cosmetic corpses ignore navigation
and do not collide, land, bounce or hurt another actor.

## Distance and crowd-aware enemy approach — 2026-11-16

The user wants enemies to rush in from far away, then slow down when close and
many enemies already pursue the player. Ordinary native enemies now approach
the player at up to 3x their configured movement speed at 120 m or farther,
easing to the nearby pace at 40 m. Nearby pace scales from the configured speed
with zero/one close pursuer to 35% with ten or more. Close pressure counts living
player pursuits within 28 m and 3.5 m vertically; distant arrivals and enemies
fighting allies do not inflate it. Clearing the crowd restores pace on the next
simulation tick. There is no hard attacker cap, waiting state or attack delay.

loading, pool or presentation objects. Saved speed values still supply the base;

## Natural player/pet 合擊 — 2026-11-16

Normal Cross Gate player melee and native pet/bear melee on one enemy within
0.35 seconds now earn a joint bonus. Count distinct participants (player required,
maximum ten); group damage after existing defenses is `sum(normal damage) *
(1 + 0.1 * participant count)`. Each later contact applies only the unpaid
difference, so 100 + 50 becomes 180 for two. Repeated contacts do not add a
participant. Skills, counters, arrows and pet-only groups get no joint bonus.
The existing separate attack-chain behavior remains in place.

native hit owner with fixed victim-local state, one shared simulation clock and
no targeting scans. Pet scattered pursuits and F/G/H orders keep their existing

order use existing bounded effect batches. Near capacity, the whole title is
omitted rather than allocating more effects or truncating letters. There is no
combat-time resource loading, new renderer, pet targeting loop or retargeting.

## Dodge / counter stats and boss retaliation — 2026-11-15

Crit, Dodge and Counter use percentage points: one run stat point adds **1%**,
not 5%. Baseline chances are 5%; existing saved character balance overrides stay

normal-damage shadow strike at the contact position. It snapshots the source
fighter's ordinary attack pose/contact; bows and kunai release one existing
pooled projectile. Left clicks, movement and normal hit recovery cannot erase

and lethal damage retires it. Counter hits are tagged through native delivery,
so player/boss counters do not start retaliation loops. Boss casts and original
specialized patterns remain in the same native owner.

## Recent additions: measured performance refactor — 2026-11-14

The Arena review found repeated long-distance reachability checks in native
target selection. Each check sampled the direct terrain corridor before using
connectivity. The public method now reuses waypoint navigation's existing proof:
connected terrain cells plus exact local entry/exit checks. Short queries still
try the direct segment first; failed component proofs retain the exact direct
fallback for narrow routes absent from the coarse grid. Target priorities,
crowding preferences, movement/contact rules, attack clocks, counts and art stay
unchanged. No new cache, targeting owner or per-species simulation was added.

Paired Play Goemon observations on the Apple M3 at 1280×800 measured the crowded
approach bucket ending at twenty seconds: native work fell from 6.78 ms to
.96–.97 ms per physics step, with target decisions falling from 6.22 ms to
.23–.25 ms. Terrain samples fell from 382 million to 4.57 million. The separate
native moving-root regression compares the original direct-first implementation:
23,274 samples versus 616 for the same sixty reachable queries. These are CPU
work savings, not an FPS multiplier; normal frame pacing stays near 60 FPS.
Shared-desktop observations are not a statistically controlled hardware study.

The newer Arena map was also excluded from the existing preparation-time
navigation warmup condition. Including it prepares the same collision/navigation
data before START, keeping the roughly 200 ms navigation rebuild out of the
first active physics step. This moves setup earlier; it does not make setup
free. Existing navigation revision checks still handle subsequent map changes.

HUD updates reuse the character's resolved loadout for skill icons, and each
cooldown query resolves its skill once. This removes repeated save validation
without caching mutable skin/equipment state. Across the nine Cross Gate
fighters, summed median HUD-update costs fell from 2,209 to 1,844 microseconds
(about 16%). Individual updates remain roughly .09–.33 ms, a smaller saving than
native route validation.

using current painterly scenery and normal spawn/contact logic. The fixture
advances the schedule to wave eleven and protects a stationary Kaz to reach

player skill use or long-session stability. Both sizes maintained the cap after
filling and passed focus, simulation-clock, event-delivery and steady frame-time
checks. Final thirty-second Standard/Large frame p95 was 17.38/17.47 ms and p99
was 18.57/18.58 ms, within the existing 25 ms p95 / 50 ms p99 limits. Warmed
node/resource counts stayed at 4,254/2,459 and 4,260/2,459 respectively. The
profiler stores frame samples, so its small memory growth is not itself a leak.

## Pets spread their replacement targets — 2026-11-13 follow-up

Automatic bears and selectable pets previously chose the nearest reachable enemy
within 18 m of themselves, with priority for enemies attacking the player. Losing
a target immediately restarted that search. Only explicit G hunts considered
other pets' existing pursuits, so an automatic pack could repeatedly converge on
the same next victim. The local-cleanup and return rules below still apply.

The shared native guard search now reuses the existing companion claim list.
Each other pet pursuing a candidate adds 5 m to its distance score; the pet's own
claim is excluded. Each candidate also gets 0–0.75 m of variation from the pet's
existing random generator. Picks are recorded immediately so later pets in the

## Current-source performance audit — 2026-11-10

Play Goemon ran the painterly source on the Apple M3 at 1280×800. The
fixed-roster mixed battles held 240 enemies and 96 allies for 60 active
seconds each. Standard averaged 77.4 FPS with a 17.7 ms p95 frame time.
Large averaged 67.6 FPS with a 17.6 ms p95. Both passed the benchmark's
55 FPS average, 25 ms p95 and 50 ms p99 gates, kept simulation in real time
and delivered all combat events. Large had two frames above 50 ms. Native
decision work took 36.0 ms in the first and native movement took 41.9 ms
across three physics steps in the next.

The launcher-default slime mode has a different workload. A 110-second
desktop run on each size let the live waves fill to 928 with the player
stationary and protected from damage so the run could reach its cap. These
runs used normal spawn rules and the default frame pacing. At 928, Standard
averaged 60.0 FPS with a 17.3 ms p95. Large averaged 31.6 FPS with an
84.3 ms p95 and had 190 frames over 50 ms. Native movement averaged
10.4–12.4 ms per physics step in the final 30 seconds on Large, versus
4.0–6.2 ms on Standard. The p95 frame measures what the player sees and
can contain several physics steps. Godot's Metal GPU timing was unavailable.

The Large repeat confirmed the slowdown with detailed profiling off.
From first reaching 928 until profiling switched on at 85 seconds,
the roughly 14-second full-roster interval averaged 13.0 FPS and had
a 132.4 ms p95. With profiling on from 85 seconds, waypoint queries
took 9.7–11.7 ms per physics step on average. In the sampled buckets,
there were roughly 680–694 waypoint calls per step, under 9% reused
an exact cached result, and no new flow fields or topology grids were
built. The next small change to test is eliminating repeated exact
connector work inside those queries, with the same routes, cap and
clearance. Keep both the frame-time test and the native navigation
comparison because they measure different things.

Starting the slime battle produced a 175 ms frame on Standard and a
346 ms frame on Large. On Large, gathering collision faces took 106 ms
and configuring native navigation took another 203 ms. The first
physics tick currently prepares both. For that hitch, reuse the existing
navigation revision check to prepare the same data while the battle
is getting ready. Keep map edits and obstacle changes invalidating it.

Freyja's Alyut route passed the Zombie Cave replay, including the Hellhound
patrol, lab boss and return. Returning outdoors through the three tested exits
took 3.36–3.43 seconds from pressing F through the sixth frame callback.
Rebuilding the map synchronously accounted for 3.16–3.21 seconds on those
returns, even after the destination was visited. Interior entries took
100–143 ms to the same callback. Profile model setup and world reconstruction
separately, then reuse the immutable destination geometry and collision where
the measurements justify it. Preserve live encounter state separately.

The 120-second Large test with 240 enemies, 96 regular allies and 24 heroes
averaged 52.0 FPS with a 28.9 ms p95 and a 34.3 ms p99. It missed the
55 FPS and 25 ms p95 gates. Up to 21 heroes attacked at once, up to 15
crescent trails were visible together, and 23 hero bodies showed trails
during the run. The recorded event phase, which includes stepping the hero
controllers, averaged 4.1 ms per physics step, versus 0.85 ms in the
native kernel. Time event delivery and hero updates separately before
changing either. Keep the combat and visual coverage gates in the replay.

The stock hero fixture hardcodes an 18 m guard radius and produced zero
hero attacks in this open-field scenario. It printed a coverage failure
but exited with status zero. The audit replay uses the production guard
radius and confirms coverage in `mixed-effects.json`. Check both that
file and the frame-time acceptance report when using this fixture.

To verify a change, run the same live-wave replay at the same resolution
and camera. Compare frames after the HUD reaches 928, then check that
all four spawn sides still deliver their waves. Keep the start and cave
transitions separate from steady frame pacing. Raw samples, replay
scripts and logs are in
`build/Other Files/Performance Audit 2026-11-10/`.

## Goemon crowd-hit lag trace — 2026-11-06 (before fix)

The user reports that Goemon feels laggy when an attack hits many enemies and
confirmed the normal left-click Gold Pipe triplet. Two separate costs reproduce
in the focused trace.
No production combat behavior, counts, assets or app export was changed.

First, the responsive player pause is short **per contact**, not per swing.
`game.gd::confirm_impact` uses max rather than addition, which protects victims
hit in the same frame. But the exact swept pipe reaches different victims on
successive frames. Each later contact rearms `player.impact_pause`; the early
return in `player.gd::_physics_process` then freezes movement and the attack
clock again. The earlier October 29 fixture tested repeated feedback within one
frame, so it did not cover this cross-frame crowd case.

Fresh isolated native-soldier results, using real 60 Hz physics callbacks and
the unchanged pipe sweep, are deterministic across two sequences per case:

| Targets arranged across the pipe arc | Sequence ticks | Paused ticks | Confirmed contacts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 78 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 85 | 7 | 3 |
| 24 | 127 | 49 | 57 |
| 80 | 140 | 62 | 113 |

Not every arranged victim intersects every stage; hit counts retain the exact
sweep, height and cover checks. Relative to one target, 24 targets add 42 frozen

first contact previously retired the projectile. The smallest change removes
that retirement and clears the homing target when it is hit, letting the bird
continue along its current heading. Existing per-bird hit history prevents
repeat hits on the same victim. Walls, three-second lifetime, damage, speed,
spread, size, timing and audio retain their existing settings. Player and
borrowed casts share this path; Kojiro is not a native NPC army kit.

native local candidate queries, precise contacts and prepared impact sparks;
there is no added target search, asset loading or new pool. More enemies hit
can produce more existing contact effects, so repeat the actual crowded
workload before making claims about army frame time or increasing capacity.

## Startup work — 2026-10-24

The user reported that launching had become slower. Fresh startup measurements
found two costs: opening the headless editor importer on every desktop launch
(**4.91 seconds** with no asset work), and checking each Wind Meadow plant
candidate against all map roads and camps while preparing the scenery.

The launcher now compares source/import metadata with the snapshot saved after
a successful import. Unchanged launches skip the editor; source additions,
edits, renames/deletions, import settings, missing/changed imported files,
class/extension caches and engine changes still refresh. The kernel lock and
standalone `--script` behavior remain intact. The full-project snapshot check
was about **0.7 seconds**. Its cache is disposable; see `docs/godot-iteration.md`.

Wind Meadow now selects nearby road segments/camps once per existing 36-metre
chunk and reuses the height already sampled for each accepted plant. Rejections
still precede the same random draws. No density, visibility range, asset,
material, collision, army count or combat setting was reduced. All **1,338
scenery MultiMesh buffers / 467,694 instance records matched the saved original
byte for byte** after the change, including the mountains after the foliage RNG.

at **7.70 seconds before and 4.60–5.34 seconds after**. Scene load through first
draw fell from **10.25 to 7.09–8.15 seconds**. These windows were unfocused;
these are startup observations, not foreground gameplay-FPS measurements.
Total launcher-to-combat-material-ready time was **16.14 seconds before and
13.88–14.71 seconds after**. The native library changed during these runs, so
each correctly refreshed imports; this is not a measured full-game repeat-launch
cache speedup. An isolated real-Godot launcher regression separately verifies
that an unchanged relaunch bypasses the importer and a new global class triggers
an import before gameplay. Do not count the later lock-rejected desktop attempt
as another successful run; a regular game was then running and was left alone.

at both supported map sizes, including chunk/road boundaries; **686** valley

checks; **63** toolkit unit tests; **12,812** imported asset checks; **98** outfit
checks; **86** structure checks; and asset preservation. Startup captures were
inspected. Existing fixture shutdown RID/resource warnings remain. No app export

## Dark Lumina 2 / Skullpion skill spikes and stomp wave — 2026-10-24

The user reported stalls when many of these bosses cast together and questioned
DL2's stomp wave. Fresh foreground profiling found several separate costs:
repeated animation setup and effect-list scans, unchanged terrain triangles being
exported again after wall damage, rebuilding their native collision tree, and
rebuilding entire route grids for each unit radius after the same obstacle change.
One instrumented wall-break frame spent about 67 ms rebuilding route grids and
47 ms refreshing navigation. These were CPU preparation costs, not permission
to remove units, reduce particles, turn off audio or lower the scenery quality.

The shared renderer now groups effect records in one pass, avoids submitting
empty batches, and seeks Skullpion's existing animation without restarting it
every frame. Stationary slope alignment is reused until the boss or terrain
changes. Collider exports reuse exact local vertices/world transforms and prune
disabled, removed or changed shapes. The native collision tree retains its
unchanged terrain prefix and rebuilds the building tail; capsule/projectile
candidates retain source order. The spherical boss sweep retains the original
edge-roundoff/tie order, and climb queries reject walls that provably cannot beat
the closest valid footing. No attack timing, damage, target checks or counts changed.

For unchanged terrain, native route grids now recertify cells/edges within the
changed obstacle's radius plus one edge. Flow fields and route certificates are
invalidated. Heights, holes, ramparts, bridge layers and domain edits still rebuild
completely. Tests compare all cached grid heights/open flags/edges and route
choices against fresh rebuilds, including both boss radii and raised layers.
Keep the original positive edge direction when checking boundary segments;
reversing a segment can change floating-point terrain samples.

## Shared character foundation — 2026-10-23

Every playable fighter uses `Hero` for movement/body ownership, health,
progression, attack attribution and the spell loadout. The dedicated and Rogue
combat controllers now inherit `scripts/character_combat.gd` for caster identity,
selection setup and focus cancellation. Goemon's weapon helpers remain on Hero
and use the same focus boundary. Unique inputs, source clocks, move rules,
rigs and animation clips remain in their character adapters.

`AttackChain` owns bounded enemy queries, exact contact dispatch, nearest swept
contacts and cover rays. Goemon/Edo/Ed/Ben/Sasuke/Yae projectile nodes use one
`CharacterProjectiles` service. It prepares visuals, restores per-use state,
clears prior targets/tickets/hits and removes a deleted caster's cached shots.
Level changes resize Goemon's existing MultiMesh batches. Musashi and Chief
keep their authored fixed-slot renderers and use the common slot lifecycle;
Rogue keeps its existing effects renderer and uses the common lease retirement
helper. Human Rogue shots now reuse that renderer's cache too. Generation
checks prevent an old flight from retiring an instance reused by a new flight.
The native C++ army and its batched presentation remain the NPC runtime.

Original event maps use `character_audio_bank.gd` for immutable samples and
weighted variants, then the existing SoundLibrary/MoveAudio playback paths.
Character-specific samples, pitch, silence and duplicate variant weights are
preserved. Changing a shared engine/helper should reach every kit; changing a
move's damage, timing, animation or sound belongs in its existing profile.

## What helped and why

1. **Use one native army simulation.** The C++ runtime owns NPC simulation;
   Godot presents it and connects it to gameplay. Avoid restoring independent
   per-unit script simulation alongside it. Moving calculations to C++ helps,
   but copying all the results into thousands of Godot objects can still cost
   more than the calculations themselves.
2. **Look nearby before doing precise work.** Spatial grids narrow melee,
   targeting, terrain and tower candidates. Keep the original precise contact,
   range, priority and visibility checks for those candidates. A fast search
   must still find the same valid hit, including at cell boundaries.
3. **Share snapshots and copy only what readers need.** Packed arrays carry
   current state between native simulation, gameplay and rendering. The current
   code defers model dictionary publication and ally field refresh until needed.
   Avoid reconstructing every enemy record for each reader or physics step.
   Preserve ownership and generation checks so retained snapshots and reused
   unit slots cannot expose stale or overwritten state.
4. **Batch drawing and presentation.** The current army renderer uses MultiMesh
   batches, baked pose data and native instance/projectile buffers. Damage
   numbers and effects use pooled presentation paths. Avoid adding a complete
   animated scene tree or fresh effect objects for every ordinary soldier/hit.
   Preserve independent animation, equipment, flashes and visible bounds.
5. **Skip unchanged work.** Reuse visibility results with proper invalidation;
   refresh only changed painterly scenery; avoid polling idle units and writing
   unchanged poses. Terrain probes for cosmetic presentation can be batched.
   Damage, deaths and gameplay events must still arrive promptly and in order.
6. **Optimize assets through the existing preservation pipeline.** Reduce
   redundant mesh/material work without changing approved art, animation,
   joints, sockets or hit regions. Follow `tools/asset_pipeline/README.md`;
   generated derivatives are rebuilt from authored sources, never hand-edited.

## Whenever changing a character or skill

The user explicitly requested these habits for all future character/skill work.
Editing a model or skill freely is fine; repeated construction during gameplay
is the cost to watch.

- Reuse compatible existing animations, combos and attack patterns before
  creating replacements. Inspect both rigs, rest poses, proportions and weapon
  attachments first. Transfer matching motion directly where possible; retarget
  differing rigs during asset preparation and correct grips, feet and posture.
  Reuse is a default, not a reason to change the requested character design.
- Follow `docs/BLENDER_PIPELINE.md`, `assets/blender/AGENTS.md` and the nearest
  asset/workbench guide. Preserve editable originals and unsaved user work;
  export through the matching GLB/animation JSON pipeline. Saving a Blender
  action alone may not update gameplay. Rebuild affected army pose bakes and
  optimized derivatives from their sources, then check preservation, motion,
  weapon contacts and rendered gameplay. Prefer prepared animation data over
  adding per-unit runtime retargeting.
- Animation transfer and attack behavior are separate. Reuse existing combat
  logic for combos where appropriate and align poses to its events; leave hit
  timing, damage, reach, cooldowns and travel owned by the controller unless
  changes are requested. Verify the transferred attack for the player and for
  simultaneous army use when applicable before claiming performance is kept.
- Set up the selected model and resources once, then reuse the character and
  play its animations. Adjust existing shader parameters for glow or color.
  Keep individual effects isolated so changing one actor cannot recolor others
  through a shared material. Occasional character-switch setup is acceptable.
- Use the existing combat, projectile and effect systems. Reuse or pool effects
  that occur frequently rather than loading assets and constructing nodes on
  every hit. Do not build new pooling infrastructure for an occasional object
  without evidence that it needs it.
- Before reusing an effect/projectile, reset its position, target, damage,
  timers, visibility and remaining per-use state. Clear obsolete callbacks and
  references; the next use must not inherit a previous target or hit.
- Changing damage or cooldown values should update skill data/logic, without
  rebuilding visual objects. Use local target queries and shared snapshots
  rather than a full-army scan or copy for each attack.
- Test repeated attacks and overlapping effects. If the army uses the skill,
  also test many units using it together. Check appearance, hit accuracy,
  timing, frame-time spikes and resource growth; compare with the same scene
  before the change. Preserve the requested design, counts and visual quality.
- Explain the relevant choice briefly while making the change, so the user
  learns how to keep new characters and skills efficient.

## What to do next time something stutters

1. Reproduce it through `/Users/eric/Desktop/Play Goemon.command`. Record the
   map, character, army counts, camera, action and whether it is a first-use hitch
   or sustained slowdown. Keep a Git checkpoint of the relevant source before
   changing it; a commit hash alone does not describe uncommitted changes.
2. Measure the same scene before and after, at the same resolution with the
   game window in the foreground and one benchmark/game process running.
   Separate shader/import warmup from steady gameplay. Save logs and captures
   under `build/Other Files/`.
3. Inspect frame times and CPU/GPU costs. About 16.7 ms per frame is 60 FPS;
   p95 and p99 show the slower frames that averages hide. Repeated physics
   catch-up steps are a clue to CPU overload. Fewer draw calls alone do not
   prove smoother gameplay. Headless tests cannot verify rendered performance.
4. Change the largest measured cost first, using existing helpers. Keep army
   counts, combat timing, player controls and scenery consistent so a smaller
   workload cannot masquerade as a faster implementation.
5. Run the focused correctness tests, then repeat the foreground measurement
   and play the original scenario. Check attacking, summoning, deaths, effects,
   hills, bridges and portals. For long battles, also check memory and resource
   growth. Keep results only if behavior and appearance remain correct.

Use `/Users/eric/Desktop/Edit Goemon.command` to edit this same project. After
native C++ changes, rebuild with `./native/terrain_math/build.sh` while the game
is closed, then refresh imports. The Play launcher refreshes changed imports.
An app export is needed only when the user requests a build or distribution.

## How to teach this in future work

Explain each change as: **what repeated work caused the delay → what we changed
→ what measurement and gameplay check show**. Define technical terms when they
first matter. Teach from the actual scene and evidence, one bottleneck at a
time. The reusable habit is: measure, remove redundant work, preserve behavior,
then measure and play again.

selection. Repeated attacks still reuse immutable geometry and owned effect
materials; there is no new effect renderer or reduced particle count.
